composition.value: Public domain in jurisdictions applying an unextended life-plus-70-year term
composition.note: Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov died in 1908. This assessment concerns the original composition, not a later edition, arrangement or this recording; it is not a worldwide rights clearance.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis).
recording.note: Commons identifies the original Victor DM-920 78-rpm set and Monteux/San Francisco sessions of 3–4 March 1942. Its CC0 tag does not independently prove that the uploader could waive Victor’s recording rights; this assessment instead uses the historic commercial recording under rule 3. Usable under the programme’s pre-1963 European sound-recording rule; the former 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence; US sound-recording status is not established. A recording date alone is not represented as an independently verified first-publication date.

rights.creditLine: Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov: Scheherazade, Op. 35, III. The Young Prince and the Young Princess — San Francisco Symphony Orchestra, Pierre Monteux; Naoum Blinder, violin. Victor DM-920, recorded 3–4 March 1942. Transfer by Bob Varney, Internet Archive, via Wikimedia Commons; the file is designated CC0, with underlying recording rights not independently cleared.
